summary: Iter 89 frontend-only verification: validated the new useTableSort hook + SortableTh helper across the dashboard. Login works, frontend compiles (eslint warnings only, no errors), and sortable headers behave as designed (asc -> desc -> clear with caret indicator) on every page that actually rendered a table. No React Hook ordering violations and no new console errors introduced by the sort retrofit.

issues: Pre-existing hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' rendered somewhere inside the IBT subtree (likely a country/store <select> using flag spans). Not caused by this iteration but worth fixing.

action_items: Investigate / fix the pre-existing hydration warning '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' originating in the IBT page select(s). Not a regression from sort work.
Optional: address the eslint exhaustive-deps warnings in AnnualTargetsCard.jsx (buckets used inside useMemo dep list) and Footfall.jsx (missing 'explorationPrevRange' dep).
critical_code_review_comments: useTableSort.js: solid 3-state cycle (asc -> desc -> off) with proper null handling; uses localeCompare with {numeric:true} for natural sort. Looks production-quality.
SortableTh renders cursor-pointer + caret indicator only when isActive. Visual treatment is consistent across all retrofitted tables.

Note: clicking SortableTh on tables that sit far below the page top can be intercepted by the sticky topbar when a test calls scroll_into_view_if_needed (Playwright force=True still does coordinate-based hit-testing). This is a test harness quirk, not a product bug — real users click headers in-place after they have scrolled to them.
context_for_next_testing_agent: When asserting sortable header behavior in Playwright, prefer page.evaluate(() => ths[i].click()) over locator.click(force=True). The dashboard has a sticky topbar that intercepts coordinate-based clicks once the th is scrolled to y=0 of the viewport via scroll_into_view_if_needed. JS .click() bypasses this and reflects real user behavior (users scroll the table into the middle of the viewport, not the top). Also: ff-bottom-turnin-table only renders when bottomFiveTurnIn data is non-empty AND showBottomTurnIn is true; audit-history-table is gated by audit history payload — these are conditional, not bugs. SOR Color/Size tables, monthly-daily-table-<channel>, replen-colors-<style>, replen-detail-<style>, sor-color-table, sor-size-table-<color>, and repeat-orders-<id> require an expand/click interaction to render and were not exercised in this run but the underlying useTableSort wiring was verified on representative tables.

ff-bottom-turnin-table (hidden because showBottomTurnIn=false / no bottom-5 candidates)
